{
  "thinking": "Blank table, 10 minutes, and the judge only sees the fallen outline. A fish has a clean silhouette and a tail fin that says 'fish' on its own, so I'll grab the pad and sketch one before anyone starts placing dominoes.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish! The outline alone reads as a fish, and the tail fan is the giveaway. I'm sketching it on the pad now, so start on the tail end and we'll grow it from there.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [8, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [12, 6], [18, 5], [22, 8], [23, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[23, 10], [22, 12], [18, 15], [12, 14], [8, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [4, 6], [3, 10], [4, 14], [8, 10]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 20, "y0": 8, "x1": 20, "y1": 7},
    {"type": "label", "x": 8, "y": 10, "text": "START"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Animal: fish, facing right. Pad: stroke 1 = top of body from tail junction to nose (START at tail junction, left). Stroke 2 = belly back from nose to tail junction. Stroke 3 = tail fin fan branching from START. Plan: trace 1 first (I take it), then 2 and 3 once they can attach. Check with Omar/Hana/Jack who can take the belly and tail."
}
